descriptions.text: Crypto detective ZachXBT stated on his Telegram channel that the Middle Eastern cryptocurrency exchange Rain appears to have been hacked, resulting in a loss of $14.8 million USD. The breach occurred on April 29, 2024, when Rain's BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP wallets experienced suspicious outflows of funds, which were quickly transferred to instant exchanges and converted into BTC and ETH.

Rain, a Bahrain-based centralized cryptocurrency exchange, disclosed a security incident after suspicious April 29, 2024 outflows drained roughly $14.8 million from wallets handling BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and ERC-20 assets. Public evidence supports a hot wallet or signing infrastructure compromise, but Rain did not publish a technical postmortem identifying the initial access path. Public reporting and Rain's statements support unauthorized access to exchange-controlled hot wallets or their signing infrastructure across multiple chains. Rain did not disclose the precise intrusion method, compromised system, or key management failure that enabled the withdrawals.

Bahrain-based cryptocurrency exchange Rain was exploited for around $16.13 million dollars on April 29. The exchange did not publicly disclose the hack until the suspicious outflows across wallets on multiple blockchains were noticed by blockchain investigator zachxbt. After zachxbt sounded the alarm on May 13, Rain admitted that they had had a "security incident", but stressed that customer funds were safe, and stated that the Rain Group had "covered any potential losses resulting from this incident". The attack was later attributed to North Korean state-sponsored attackers.
